```{r}
#| include: false
# scripts/render_docs.sh copies tests/fixtures/tiny into SCX_DOCS_WORK, so
# the code below can name the files directly. Python cells come from
# _convert-py.qmd, rendered by Jupyter in its own process.
work <- Sys.getenv("SCX_DOCS_WORK")
if (!nzchar(work)) stop("SCX_DOCS_WORK is not set: render with scripts/render_docs.sh")
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = work)
```

This page takes one small H5Seurat file, looks inside it, converts it to
AnnData `.h5ad`, and checks the result. Each step is shown three ways: with
the `scx` command line, with the Python package and with the R package. All
three call the same engine, so they detect the same formats and use the same
defaults.

The example file, `tiny_v4.h5seurat`, is a 6-cell by 5-gene dataset from the
SCX test fixtures. The second cell has no counts and two genes are each
expressed in a single cell, so empty cells and sparse genes are part of the
example.

## Look before converting

`inspect` reads only metadata: the format, the shape, the column names and
the embedding keys. The count matrix is not loaded, whatever the file size.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## CLI

```{bash}
scx inspect tiny_v4.h5seurat
```

## Python

{{< embed _convert-py.qmd#py-inspect echo=true >}}

## R

```{r}
library(picklerick)

info <- inspect("tiny_v4.h5seurat")
info[c("format", "n_obs", "n_vars", "obs_cols")]
```

:::

## Convert

The input format is detected from the file's content; the output format is
chosen by the extension of the output path. The matrix is streamed in chunks
of 5000 cells by default, so peak memory does not grow with the number of
cells.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## CLI

```{bash}
scx convert tiny_v4.h5seurat tiny_cli.h5ad
```

## Python

{{< embed _convert-py.qmd#py-convert echo=true >}}

## R

```{r}
convert("tiny_v4.h5seurat", "tiny_r.h5ad")
```

:::

## Check the result

The converted file has the same shape and cell metadata as the source.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## CLI

```{bash}
scx inspect tiny_cli.h5ad
```

## Python

{{< embed _convert-py.qmd#py-check echo=true >}}

## R

```{r}
sce <- read_h5ad("tiny_r.h5ad")
sce
```

:::

## Options shared by all three

| Option | CLI | Python | R | Default |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cells per streamed chunk | `--chunk-size` | `chunk_size=` | `chunk_size =` | 5000 |
| Output matrix type | `--dtype` | `dtype=` | `dtype =` | `f32` |
| Seurat assay to read (H5Seurat input) | `--assay` | `assay=` | `assay =` | `RNA` |
| Seurat layer to read (H5Seurat input) | `--layer` | `layer=` | `layer =` | `counts` |

The full lists are in each reference: `scx convert --help`,
`picklerick.convert` and `?picklerick::convert`.
